description: Canonical argument names for driving a sample app from automation. Names are identical on all four platforms; only the delivery mechanism differs. A drawer is for humans, launch arguments are for machines — ship both.

args.name: scenario
args.values: any flow scenario id from scenarios.json

args.name: theme
args.values: any theme scenario id from scenarios.json

args.name: route
args.description: Which entry route hosts the SDK flow. The in-shell route is the one that exposes host-chrome and inset defects; the fullscreen route cannot.

args.name: autostart
args.values: a product id from scenarios.json products, or null to stay on the home screen
args.description: Starts a flow immediately on launch, so a flow does not have to tap its way in. The product `id` rather than its `jobType`, matching every other id reference in spec/; it lands directly on the flow route named by `route`, skipping the pre-flow forms.

args.name: seedJobs
args.description: Seeds the design's eleven fixture verifications, as a precondition for flows that need a populated list. The app seeds nothing on its own: a stored row claims a verification was submitted, and eleven that never were would sit among a partner's real ones for good. But no UI path creates a row without a successful submission — which needs a real token and a valid sandbox identity — so a device flow covering the list, its filters, select mode or removal has no other way to arrive at one. Idempotent: the rows are keyed by job id and re-seeding is a no-op, and because they persist, one seeded launch covers every later step in the same flow. Present in release builds too, deliberately: the device suite has to pass on the minified, resource-shrunk variant as well as debug, and that run needs the same precondition. It seeds nothing unless asked, so a partner build behaves exactly as it would without the argument.

args.name: seedProfiles
args.description: Seeds the design's three fixture profiles in place of the single empty profile a plain launch carries, as a precondition for flows that assert on the profile list, the switch sheet or a fixture's configuration screen. The app seeds nothing on its own: the active profile's organisation is what the SDK's consent screen shows as the partner, and its id is the partner id the SDK is handed when no token session is linked, so a fictional profile on a partner's device is fabricated data rather than decoration. Profiles live in memory, so unlike seedJobs the argument has to be passed on every launch that needs them; a cold start by deep link carries no arguments and therefore shows the one empty profile. Present in release builds too, for the same reason as seedJobs.

args.name: probes
args.description: Reveals the on-screen probe affordances — the result card and its callback counters — on a release build. Always on in debug, so the argument is only ever needed by a release run. It exists because the affordances are how a flow observes what the SDK did, and the release variant is the one where consumption defects surface: hiding them from release outright would mean half the device suite could only run on the configuration that proves the least. A partner opening the app sees nothing; the code still ships, minified and shrunk, on the release classpath — never compiled out with a debug-only source set, which would also make this argument impossible. It does NOT reveal the Settings DEBUG section (the Scenarios row): that is strictly debug-only on every platform, because no flow needs it — they deep-link to the drawer — and a partner should never find a scenario picker in Settings on any build.

args.name: appLocale
args.description: In-app locale override. Needed because changing the device locale is not reliably scriptable on every OEM.

args.name: holdCamera
args.description: Host acquires the camera before handing off, to test contention. Verify the host actually acquired it before concluding anything — a probe that never acquired the camera passes vacuously.

args.name: noticeWindow
args.description: How long a transient notice stays before dismissing itself. Exists because a notice that offers an action is a race for automation: the default window is short enough not to outlive its cause, so on a loaded runner a flow can wait for the action, tap it, and have the tap land after the notice has gone — and the offer is consumed on dismissal, so there is no second chance to retry. A flow that has to act on a notice sets this; a flow whose subject IS the auto-dismiss must not, or it stops testing the timer. Not set by an ordinary launch, so a partner build behaves exactly as it would without the argument.

mechanisms.android: Intent extras: adb shell am start -e scenario expiredToken -e route shell, or Maestro's launchApp `arguments`. Force-stop the app first, and then reach the screen under test by tapping rather than by deep link: an intent sent to a live task carries FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK, which rebuilds the Activity around the new intent and resets these arguments to their defaults. Device-measured 2026-08-14; a deep link taken mid-run therefore reads as a parsing bug when it is a task-lifecycle one.
mechanisms.ios: Launch arguments read through UserDefaults: app.launchArguments = ["-scenario", "expiredToken"]. XCUITest sets them directly.
mechanisms.flutter: Cold-start deep link, read through PlatformDispatcher.defaultRouteName — the engine's own launch route, so the app carries no deep-link package at all. Terminate the app first: that value is read once in main(), before the first frame, so a link delivered to a live app navigates but never re-seeds arguments. Settled 2026-08-27 rather than reading intent extras and NSUserDefaults through a MethodChannel, because a native shim in a Dart-first SDK contradicts what that SDK is for. CORRECTED 2026-09-21: this said 'read through app_links', which was never true — the app has no such dependency, and a device flow written against a package that is not there has nothing to attach to.
mechanisms.expo: Cold-start deep link, read through expo-linking: terminate the app first, then parse arguments from getInitialURL() only, never from the url event listener — a link delivered to a live app must never re-seed arguments. Settled 2026-08-27, same reasoning as flutter — a TypeScript-first SDK should not need a native module to be automatable.

notes: Read once, from the launch itself — the launching intent on Android and iOS, the cold-start link on Flutter and Expo — and applied once: a recreation re-reads the same launch source, so re-seeding would discard whatever the drawer selected after launch.

DELIVERY IS PER-PLATFORM BY DECISION, not for want of a ruling — settled 2026-08-27 against a single cross-platform mechanism. The contract this file owns is the NAMES; delivery was always allowed to differ, and the description above says so. One uniform deep-link mechanism was rejected because of the trap recorded under `android`: an intent into a live task resets every argument, and flows already deep-link mid-run to reach the scenario drawer, so arguments arriving by link would collide with the drawer in all four apps and the fix would be a subtle first-link-only invariant replicated four times. Android and iOS keep their native mechanisms, which no drawer link can disturb. Flutter and Expo take a cold-start link because the alternative is a native shim in the two SDKs whose value proposition is not needing one — and they generalise, to all nine names, exactly what Android already does for `probes` below.

Parse all nine names even where a build cannot act on one yet, so the four apps accept the same surface. `scenario`, `theme`, `route`, `autostart`, `seedJobs`, `seedProfiles` and `probes` take effect on their own; `appLocale` and `holdCamera` configure the handoff to the SDK and take effect where that handoff is built.

`probes` has one platform-specific addition, and it is not optional: on Android it is read from the launching URI's query string as well as from the intent extras. A deep link arrives as an ACTION_VIEW intent that carries no extras, and four of the eight flows reach the result card that way — so on release the card would be hidden and those runs could only ever pass on debug. Only this argument is read from the link; letting a link seed the others would contradict the rule above that a deep link resets them. Appending `?probes=true` to a route whose pattern declares no query is safe on androidx.navigation: a non-parameterised deep-link pattern terminates its path regex with `($|(\?(.)*)|(#(.)*))`, and a parameterised one matches only the names its own pattern declares. Each platform needs its own answer to the same problem — a link is how automation arrives.

There is no `sandbox` argument, and adding one back would be a regression. Removed 2026-08-24 with the app's environment control: the session token's `api_url` claim decides the environment, so nothing can override it and no app has a toggle to pin. The rule it replaces — automation must never run with sandbox=false — now holds by construction rather than by discipline, because automation mints its own unsigned fixture tokens and one naming the production host still submits nothing. A run proves where it went on `sample_result_environment`.

An unrecognised value falls back to that argument's default rather than failing the launch. That is only safe because the result card publishes what the run actually got — assert on sample_result_active_scenario, never on the argument you passed.
openDecisions: Preferred: one cross-platform entry point via a deep link, drivable from adb, simctl and a device flow on all four platforms, with the native mechanisms above kept as the platform-specific alternate. The scheme is per app and already assigned in app-identity.json (e.g. usesmileid-sample-android://run?scenario=…&route=…) because two apps sharing a scheme break automation. Confirm the query-parameter shape when the first two apps land, then delete this note.
Credentials are seeded as arguments, never typed: keyboard input drops characters from long API keys.
